findings: The four largest recorded bbox losses are28,15,23,26grains at21.0,21.1,21.2,21.3s (92total); three remaining bbox grains exit by21.4s. These are sampled net occupancy changes, not exact continuous flux.

During21.0–21.4s the observed bowl surface centroid is projected inside the20.995mm receiver radius (11.357→2.195mm radial offset). The entire rim footprint is only partly over the aperture until21.4s: maximum rim radius31.490→20.574mm.

The lowest-rim-vertex outlet proxy is INSIDE at each main-burst sample:17.279,16.515,15.489,16.728,18.239mm radial, roughly42–43mm above the receiver rim. At20.8/20.9s it is slightly outside(22.732/22.187mm), before the large losses.

Frozen commanded waypoint centroid offset is approximately1.784mm during the mainburst. Thus the commanded rigid root poses compensate the long bowl offset; evidence does not support a simple claim that an uncompensated fixed-root rotation sweeps the entire bowl away from the receiver.

Observed root-to-active-waypoint endpoint error reaches29.868mm during21.0s and rim overhang persists, but a moving endpoint tracking error is not a measured collision failure or a proof of bad control.

Geometric evidence narrows the question to partial overhang, outlet margin, elevated release and post-release motion/deflection. A projected lowest vertex inside the aperture does not guarantee grain landing inside; no unique causal claim is possible without exact sub-sample release/contact evidence.
